newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss ban guns for Algerians to stop rebel arming.
newsitem.headline: Swiss ban guns for Algerians to stop rebel arming.

text.p: Switzerland on Monday barred Algerians from buying guns or ammunition in order to stem weapons supplies to Islamic fundamentalist guerrillas, Berne's justice ministry said.

"The reason for this measure is the discovery from various cases that Algerian citizens in Switzerland bought firearms and ammunition systematically and in an organised fashion and smuggled them to their home country," a ministry statement said.

It said there were grounds to believe that supporters of Algeria's Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) and Armed Islamic Group (GIA) could step up arms procuring in Switzerland, where no special permit is needed to buy guns.

Algeria has been battered by bloody conflicts and massacres since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. About 60,000 people have died in the five years of violence.
"In addition, it cannot be ruled out based on recent developments in Algeria that violent conflicts will increasingly be fought abroad and therefore also in Switzerland," the ministry added.

The decree issued by the Federal Council, or cabinet, also prohibited Algerian nationals from carrying weapons in public, a right granted to Swiss and legal aliens in half the country's 26 cantons or states.
"With this decree, the Federal Council intends to safeguard important foreign policy interests as well as ensure peace, order and security in Switzerland," the ministry said.
Until now, Algerians with Swiss residency papers could buy guns just as easily as Swiss nationals and other legal aliens by simply presenting an ordinary identification card.

The ban for Algerians is the fourth such measure in six years. Berne barred gun purchases and carrying by citizens of former Yugoslavia at the start of the war there in 1991. It did the same with Turks in 1993 and Sri Lankans in 1995.
